To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electronic structure of the Mn impurity atoms in Ga1-xMnxAs is modified by post-growth annealing and that this modification is caused by the diffusion of Mn atoms from the bulk of the sample towards its surface where the Mn atoms are passivated by the surface oxygen.

post-annealing induces the diffusion of Mn atoms from interstitial sites into the surface of Ga1−x−MnxAs and the oxidation of these surface Mn impurity atoms by oxygen, which is evidenced by resonant in-elastic x-ray scattering.
the Mn impurity atoms in Ga1-xMnxAs epifilms are passivated by surface oxidation, and that the passivation process is enhanced by post-annealing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure of the Mn impurities in GaAs host lattice, and its dependence on the annealing temperature.
the electronic structure of as grown and annealed Ga1−yMyMnxAs (M=Al and Ga, y=0.05 and 0.10, x=0.055).
the study of the electronic structure of Ga1−x MnxAs epilayer using x-ray emission and absorption spectroscopy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mn atoms in the as-grown Ga1−x−MnxAs are located in interstitial positions in a GaAs host lattice and are passivated by As atoms.

post-annealing at 500–600 °C induces a diffusion of Mn impurities from the interstitial positions in GaAs lattice to the surface, where they are oxidized and passivated by oxygen, which is the origin of the observed increase of the L2/L3 intensity ratio in Mn L2, 3 x-ray emission.
the post-annealing process leads to the diffusion of the interstitial Mn impurities to the surface where the oxygen atoms passivate the Mn atoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the post-annealed Mn atoms are in a higher oxidation state, and the Mn 3d electrons are more localized than those of as-grown samples.
the Mn L2, 3-emission spectra are useful to probe the electronic structure and oxidation state of Mn impurity in Ga1− xMnxAs.
post-annealing of Ga1−x Mn xAs epilayers results in the diffusion of Mn atoms to the surface and their subsequent passivation by oxygen, which leads to a reduction of the Mn 3d band width.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic structure of the Mn impurity atoms can be modified by the post-annealing process.
the Mn L3 emission intensity can be used as a measure of Mn passivation in Ga1− xMnxAs.
the Mn L3 emission line is more sensitive to the oxidation than the L2 line.
